narrative_purpose: Recreates the observation that founded chronobiology: a mimosa continues opening and closing on schedule after the external light cycle has been removed, revealing that the rhythm is generated inside the organism.
subject: The same potted Mimosa pudica appears in three adjacent observations inside a completely closed eighteenth-century wooden cupboard. In the first, its compound leaves are spread open despite total darkness; in the second, hours later, the leaflets are folded together; in the third, the following internal morning, they are open again. The cupboard door remains shut in every view, and a thin seal of dust along its edge is undisturbed. A small mechanical pocket watch sits outside the cupboard, never inside with the plant.
scene: Jean-Jacques d'Ortous de Mairan's quiet Paris study in 1729, rendered as a repeated naturalist observation rather than a staged portrait; the plant is the only living subject.
camera: Matched front-on cutaway views through the cupboard wall, identical framing and scale across all three states.
light: The cupboard interior stays deep indigo with only faint cyan explanatory edge light on the leaves; a restrained amber glow outside the sealed door marks changing time without illuminating the plant.
palette: Void indigo wood interior, muted teal leaves, pale cyan edges, sparse amber confined outside the cupboard.
style: Painterly historical botany plate with tactile wood, soil and leaf texture; observational and restrained.
detail_level: Crisp repeated leaf postures and sealed cupboard edge; room furniture is soft and secondary.
composition: Three equal cupboard windows run left to right: open leaves, folded leaves, open leaves. The surrounding room and watch occupy a narrow lower strip. Leave dark space beside each leaf crown for callouts.
consistency_notes: Use the exact same plant, pot and sealed cupboard in all three observations. Only leaf posture and the external time glow may change; the interior must remain dark.
negative_prompt: no text, no clocks with readable numbers, no arrows, no open cupboard, no light beam inside, no modern laboratory, no photographic or CGI look
